title: Should padding be respected on "natively styled" form controls?
body:
Consider:

```
data:text/html,<button style="padding: 20px;">Foo</button><select style="padding: 20px"><option>Bar
```

The behavior is all over the place:

 * WebKit ignores the padding altogether.
 * Chrome respects the author padding, _but_ adds some magical extra padding, only to `<select>`.
 * Firefox respects the author padding.

With `appearance: none`, all browsers respect the author padding.

My intuition is that given `padding` is not one of the properties that disable native appearance, it should be respected as is (that is, that the Firefox behavior is preferable).

Firefox used to have magical "extra" padding on `<select>` _regardless of native appearance_ which was removed in bug [1560824](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1560824) and bug [1582545](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1582545) for the block and inline directions respectively.

The [Chrome code](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/layout/layout_theme_default.cc;l=226-232;drc=2899fd9a2767ef605edff106d1e00ff45af08a2e) claims to match (old) Firefox behavior, but it never did (because Firefox did this regardless of appearance).

My preference is to match current Firefox behavior, though ignoring `padding` could also be an option (rather unfotunate IMO, tho). What Chrome is doing for `<select>` seems rather bespoke. However, I'm curious about thoughts from others and whether we could reach interop here.
